speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how does the Ministry ensure that lorries that carry sand do cover them up to prevent spillage on the roads while moving; and (b) for lorries that are found not to have done so, what are the penalties that are imposed on them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Sand or other materials spilt from improperly covered lorries on public roads can endanger the safety of motorists and dirty our environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) engages sand suppliers and commercial transport companies to remind their drivers to be vigilant in keeping sand covered during transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Commercial transport companies are also reminded to inspect their lorry fleets regularly for faulty cargo flap covers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Members of the public who witness sand spillage on public roads should report the incident to NEA.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the roads, I very often see vehicles carrying sand – both wet and dry – overloaded with these items: sand, gravel, stones.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These pose a real danger to other vehicle users and even people.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can NEA consider working with the Ministry of Transport to deploy road surveillance technology to monitor such vehicles and take enforcement action where necessary?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, NEA does stakeouts along public roads to spot and act against such errant vehicles and drivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA), on the other hand, conducts routine patrols and operations to enforce against overloaded vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In my constituency, there are thousands of such heavy laden vehicles plying the road.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unfortunately, the feedback I have is that they are either uncovered or they are spilling debris all over the road.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Every day that I drive on the road, I see a lot of such vehicles that are in breach.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The other thing is whether the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) or NEA could consider from the origin of the journey, make it mandatory for the contractor that loads the sand to carry out an inspection before the vehicle can even go out.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: That means, the contractor checks and ensures that the vehicle is properly covered and everything is secured before the vehicle even goes out.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And if any vehicle is caught in breach, we not only go after the driver, but we also go after the contractor that allowed the vehicle to get out of the worksite in the first place.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, as I have said earlier, any member of the public who actually observes such spillage on the road can report it to NEA.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I had also noted, NEA does stakeouts as well as deploy portable cameras for surveillance of such acts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the Member could follow up with NEA on the area that he is talking about.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards the responsibility, as I have also said, upstream, we work with the commercial transport operators as well as the sand suppliers and remind them to inspect their lorry fleets frequently while making sure that their flap covers are operational.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is why our Act makes them responsible, but we work with the vehicle owners to identify who the particular drivers are.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, we will continue to see how we can engage with the commercial transport operators as well as the sand and building material suppliers upstream.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
